subject: HoloHealth — deployment pathway & dedicated sizing options (post-demo)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Locke <ethan.locke@holohealth.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@holohealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HoloHealth — deployment pathway & dedicated sizing options (post-demo)

Thanks again for the demo this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can size Dedicated correctly and confirm if Hosted / Dedicated / Private is the right fit for HoloHealth.

Recap (high-level)
- Primary workload: real-time clinical summarization + patient QA for your telehealth product. Models invoked both for short prompts (clinical triage) and long-context summarization (visit notes).
- Data residency: US-only; some PHI covered workloads (needs VPC + KMS).
- Current traffic expectation (what we heard on the call): bursty daytime traffic, peak ~150 QPS, baseline ~40 QPS.

Open questions for sizing & deployment choice (can you confirm?):
1) Peak concurrent requests you expect during worst-case hour? (We heard ~150 QPS but need concurrency target and acceptable 95th percentile latency)
2) Typical prompt / response token mix: split between short (<=128 tokens) vs long (>512 tokens) flows and average response tokens.
3) Tolerance for cold-starts and requirement for KV cache persistence across requests.
4) Preference on GPU families (H100 vs A100) or budget constraints we should assume.

Attached a capacity workbook with a few scenarios (short/medium/long prompt mixes and 3 GPU mixes). If you can fill the highlighted cells this week we’ll run an internal sizing estimate and propose a Dedicated pool configuration + fallback plan to Hosted for overflow.

Next steps
- Priya / Ethan: please complete the highlighted tab in holohealth-capacity-workbook.xlsx (I attached) or reply with the split for short/medium/long prompts and target p95 latency.
- We'll schedule a 60-min sizing workshop next week (please propose 2x 1-hour windows).

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: Re: HoloHealth — deployment pathway & dedicated sizing options (post-demo)

Thanks Karthik — good summary. Quick answers inline.

> 1) Peak concurrent requests you expect during worst-case hour?
We typically size for peak QPS. Best estimate now: peak ~160 requests/sec (observed during marketing pushes), baseline ~45 req/sec. For latency SLO we want p95 < 550ms for short prompts and p95 < 1.5s for long summarization flows.

> 2) Typical prompt / response token mix
Approx split: short triage prompts 60% (avg req: 40 input tokens / 80 output tokens), medium follow-ups 25% (avg 150 in / 200 out), long summarization 15% (avg 1200 input / 700 output).

> 3) Tolerance for cold-starts and KV cache persistence
We need warm hot paths for the triage flow — cold-starts causing >1s extra latency are unacceptable. We can tolerate some cold starts for batch summarization. KV cache persistence across nodes is preferred (session affinity is OK).

> 4) Preference on GPU families
We don’t have a hard preference but are cost-conscious. If you can show cost/latency tradeoffs between H100 and A100 for our token mix that would help.

I filled the short tab of the workbook with our splits and the p95 targets — attaching the version we edited.

Ethan

Forwarding Ethan's responses and workbook — flagged a few things we need to check before proposing nodes.

Flags / internal questions:
- Their long summarization workload has large input (+1200 tokens) and non-trivial output (700 tokens). That increases memory and KV cache pressure — need to understand whether we should recommend model quantization or a larger memory GPU.
- Peak 160 QPS with 60% short prompts implies heavy small-req traffic that benefits from continuous batching. We should size for sustained TPS and headroom (recommend 25–30% buffer).
- Security: they explicitly said PHI and US-only residency — this pushes toward Dedicated in a Private VPC (or Private deployment). We need to list what our private deployment package includes for KMS/HSM and audit logs.

Ben — can you draft two sizing options:
A) Cost-optimized: A100-based pool (x nodes) with auto-burst to Hosted for overflow; include expected p95 numbers for their token mix.
B) Performance-first: H100-based pool (x nodes) sized to meet p95 targets without fallback and with KV cache persistence.

Include assumptions (batch sizes, concurrency, token throughput) and a short note on which workloads we’d pin to hot nodes vs best-effort.

Thanks — Laura

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HoloHealth — deployment pathway & dedicated sizing options (post-demo)

Thanks — ran quick estimates against their submitted token mix. High level recommendation below (will produce formal worksheet next):

A) Cost-optimized (A100-40GB mix)
- Suggested pool: 6 x A100-40GB (multi-tenant Dedicated pool) with continuous batching tuned for small prompts (batch target 32 for triage workloads).
- Expected steady-state: baseline ~45 req/s comfortably; with 25% buffer this supports ~120–125 req/s at p95 targets for short prompts.
- Long summarization: large context will be slower; recommend routing summarization to a small set of pinned nodes (1–2 nodes) with higher memory reservation, or use model quantization to reduce memory (with slight quality trade-off).
- Cost note: lower hourly node price but may need Burst to Hosted for exceeding ~125 req/s.

B) Performance-first (H100-80GB mix)
- Suggested pool: 4 x H100-80GB (dedicated VPC) + 1 hot spare for redundancy. H100 enables larger batch sizes and better throughput on long-context models.
- Expected capacity: with continuous batching + async KV cache pinned for triage, this config should comfortably meet their peak 160 req/s with p95 short < 350–450ms and p95 long < 1.2–1.4s (depending on model choice).
- For KV cache persistence: configure session affinity and allocate dedicated cache memory per node; for persistent multi-node cache we can enable sharded cache (adds complexity).

Operational recommendations (both options)
- Autoscaling policy: keep reserved pool sized for 85–90% of observed peak, allow auto-burst to Hosted API for sustained overflow beyond 180 req/s.
- Latency SLOs: instrument per-route metrics and set regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Security: for Private VPC option add KMS integration + audit log retention 1yr (SOC2 evidence attached).

Next step: I'll finalize a worksheet with simulated qps curves, expected token/hr, and estimated monthly costs for both options. Recommend scheduling a 60-min capacity workshop with their infra lead and our infra engineer to lock down concurrency targets and GPU family.

If we want to be conservative I’d propose presenting both and emphasizing the H100 option if they prioritize latency over unit cost.
